title: Substantial risk
summary: Woman in her 30s with bipolar affective disorder, four weeks after a six-week informal admission for a severe depressive episode, under a home treatment team and supported most days by her sister. Schedule 6 mental descriptors give about 12 points (13(c), 16(c)), with activity 15 in conflict (15(b) would take her to 21), and no Schedule 7 descriptor is clearly met. The case turns on the consultant's opinion that work-related activity with the possibility of sanction would carry a substantial risk of relapse and self-neglect: this supports Sch 9 para 4 and, if LCW is not reached on points (reg 39(7)), Sch 8 para 4. The Sch 8 para 4(2)(b) medication exception is arguably not engaged because lithium is not yet therapeutic and the 2024 relapse happened while she was adherent; 4(2)(a) workplace adjustments are not addressed. Weakness: the consultant does not address the least onerous forms of work-related activity, which the adviser has asked about.
exercises: Sch 9 para 4 substantial risk from work-related activity
Sch 8 para 4 as fallback where LCW not met on points (reg 39(7))
Sch 8 para 4(2): medication and reasonable adjustments exceptions
reg 40(6): Sch 9 para 4 only if LCWRA not met on assessment
frequently vs majority of the time (13(c) vs 13(b) / Sch 7 descriptor 11)
prompting not in the claimant's presence does not meet Sch 7 15(c)/(d)
conflict: UC50 'I don't go out' vs sister's account of trips to the shop alone
historic hypomania not relevant to current activity 17

conditions_in_documents: Bipolar affective disorder, current episode severe depression without psychotic symptoms

activities.draft_note: Poor concentration when reading is not a sensory impairment; activity 7 does not apply.
Morning drowsiness from quetiapine is not an episode of lost or altered consciousness.

must_find.quote: I can learn things but it takes longer at the moment.
Insight good. Concentration poor.

gaps: Slower learning and poor concentration are recorded but nothing suggests she cannot learn a moderately complex task.

must_find.quote: sister says before admission she found the hob left on after client made soup, once. Nothing since discharge.

gaps: One pre-admission incident; no current evidence that she requires supervision to maintain safety.
activities.draft_note: Single historic incident does not support a descriptor.

must_find.quote: I mean to have a shower and get dressed and I don't.
Sister says "three or four days a week" she has not washed or dressed when she arrives.
I don't open my post, she opens it.
sister reports she showered that morning because of the appointment.
Client heats meal in microwave if sister reminds her by text; some days doesn't eat until sister arrives.

gaps: Three or four days a week is frequent but not clearly the majority of the time, so 13(b) and Sch 7 descriptor 11 are not made out on current evidence; a diary would show which side of the line she is.
Unclear how much the sister's texts and the HTT calls are doing; evidence of what happens without prompting would strengthen the activity.
activities.draft_note: Frequent failure to initiate washing, dressing, meals and post, due to depression; 13(c), 6 points.

must_find.quote: I don't really have a routine just now. If something is different I get stressed.
HTT changed visit time without notice once, client did not answer.

gaps: One example of an unplanned change; no evidence that day to day life is made significantly more difficult overall. Adviser notes the activity is weak.

must_find.quote: I don't go out. My sister takes me to appointments.
Sister says she has been to the corner shop on her own "two or three times" since discharge for milk and cigarettes
Has not been to the GP or pharmacy on her own since discharge; says she would not manage, "I'd turn back". Not tested.
She attends appointments only when accompanied by her sister.

gaps: The corner shop trips mean 15(a) cannot apply and undercut the UC50's 'I don't go out'.
15(b) needs evidence that she is unable (not just unwilling or never tried) to get to a specified familiar place unaccompanied; her own prediction 'I'd turn back' is untested.
No evidence about unfamiliar places beyond appointments with her sister.
activities.draft_note: Arguable 15(b) (9 points) but the evidence conflicts and is untested; left for the expert. If accepted, the total reaches 21 and LCW is met on points.

must_find.quote: I don't answer the door unless I know who it is. When there's a new person from the crisis team I find it really hard.
has found visits from unfamiliar home treatment staff distressing.
Sister says when a new worker came she would not let them in on one occasion, sister had to come round.
Spoke to me but would not have agreed to see me without sister present

gaps: She did engage with the adviser (with her sister present), so 16(b) 'always precluded' is not supported.
Only one recorded refusal of an unfamiliar worker; frequency of distress with strangers could be clarified from HTT notes.
activities.draft_note: Consistent evidence from client, consultant and sister of significant distress with unfamiliar people; 16(c), 6 points.

must_find.quote: When I'm high I can be a bit much, but I'm not like that now.
Nothing like that now or since 2019.

gaps: Disinhibited behaviour is historic (2019 hypomania); nothing current.
activities.draft_note: Historic only; no descriptor applies at present.

must_find.quote: Other days she has, sometimes because sister texted to remind her.

gaps: Would need evidence that she cannot reliably initiate or complete two sequential personal actions on the majority of occasions (reg 40(4)); current evidence is three or four days a week.
activities.draft_note: Not met on current evidence; revisit if a diary shows the majority of days.

must_find.quote: Has stopped replying to friends' messages.

gaps: Social contact is not always precluded: she sees her sister daily, engaged with the adviser and with clinicians.

must_find.quote: Sometimes I forget to eat.
During the first three weeks of admission nursing staff needed to prompt her to eat and to attend to personal care.
client says she "would eat something, toast or whatever".

gaps: Prompting in her presence was needed during admission, but that has resolved; current prompting is by text and phone, which is not 'in the claimant's presence' for 15(c) or 15(d).
activities.draft_note: 15(c)/(d) not met at present; relevant history for the self-neglect risk argument.

must_not_claim: She has current thoughts of self-harm or a history of self-harm (the consultant records no current thoughts of harm and no intent on admission; no history is documented).
She was detained under the Mental Health Act (the admission was informal).
She had psychotic symptoms (both letters say without psychotic symptoms).
A sanction was applied to her UC (she received a warning letter; the notes say no sanction was applied as far as she knows).
She has been allocated a care coordinator or CPN (a CMHT referral has been made; none is allocated yet).
There is a risk to other people (the consultant says there is no identified risk to others).
